protocol.cold: Clear only the derived catalogue cache before every measured query; OS/file caches are not flushed.
protocol.warm: Prime the same request once immediately before each timed retrieval; only hourly state is reusable, query-route reuse is disabled.
protocol.timed_region: generator.retrieve only; excludes prime, cache clearing, parity, RSS and JSON work
protocol.memory: Same process with both input generators loaded; all caches cleared between passes. RSS is whole-process and cannot be attributed to a single generator.
protocol.rss_sampling: At pass boundaries and after each query; temporary allocation peaks may be missed.
protocol.cpu_measurement: Per-query process CPU readings can be quantized by OS accounting, especially on Windows, and their sum may undercount short queries. Zero denominators produce a null CPU ratio. Whole-pass CPU is also reported but includes prime/setup/checks.
protocol.labels: No labels are deserialized or used. TemporalStore integrity verification hashes source files, including label-file bytes.
protocol.statistical_scope: Observed ratios of paired local runs, without a population-level speedup confidence interval.

limitations: CPU desktop load is uncontrolled; these are local observations, not production capacity.
Retrieval microbenchmark omits HTTP, JSON, queueing and optional v3 reranking.
Cold means derived state cold, not a cold process or a cold OS page cache.
Warm timings exclude an explicit per-query priming request; priming cost must be paid in a real service.
